#AI Query Rewriter: Turn Plain-Language Questions into PubMed Searches

Product: Biblion Citation Assistant (AI feature)

Audience: Academic Researchers, Clinicians & Bioinformaticians

Requires: A Biblion account with an active trial or subscription, and your own API key from an AI provider

Maintained by: Documentation Writer

#1. What It Does and Why You Would Use It

Good PubMed searches need boolean logic, MeSH headings and field tags such as [Title/Abstract]. The AI Query Rewriter converts a plain-language description into a well-formed PubMed query, and shows it to you before anything is searched.

Example

You typeBiblion proposes
p53 mutation in non-small cell lung cancer("genes, p53"[MeSH Terms] OR "p53 mutation"[Title/Abstract]) AND ("carcinoma, non-small-cell lung"[MeSH Terms] OR "non-small cell lung cancer"[Title/Abstract])

Value to you: better recall (synonyms and MeSH terms you might forget), fewer irrelevant hits, and a reusable query you can read, edit and learn from. You stay in control: nothing is searched until you click apply.

#2. Bring Your Own Key (BYOK)

Biblion does not run the AI model for you. You connect your own account with one of these providers:

  • OpenRouter (access to many models with one key)
  • OpenAI
  • Anthropic
  • Gemini

You pay your provider directly for usage, usually a tiny amount per query. Your key is never displayed in full again; Biblion only shows a masked hint such as sk-or-...1234.

#3. Set Up (One Time)

  1. Sign in to Biblion (Account & Sign-In).
  2. Click your name in the header, then AI Settings.
  3. In AI Query Rewriter Settings, choose your provider.
  4. Enter the model name (for OpenRouter, for example anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet).
  5. Paste your API key.
  6. Click Save Settings. A green message confirms Settings saved successfully. Close the dialog.

Setting up while registering: the Create Account form has an optional AI section where you can choose a provider and paste a key right away.

#4. Rewrite and Search

  1. On the Search page, type your question in the search box.
  2. Click the AI Rewrite button next to the search box.
  3. A preview dialog opens showing:
  • your original text,
  • the rewritten query in an editable box, and
  • a Valid Syntax badge confirming balanced parentheses and valid field tags.
  1. Edit the query if you like.
  2. Click Apply & Search PubMed. The search box is filled with the new query and results appear.

#5. When the Rewritten Query Finds Nothing

An AI-written query can occasionally be too strict. If it returns zero results, Biblion shows an Automatic Term Mapping Fallback card explaining that the strict boolean query returned 0 hits. Click the fallback button to run your original text through PubMed's own Automatic Term Mapping instead. The search box returns to your original wording and results are shown.

#6. Troubleshooting

MessageWhat it meansWhat to do
Upstream Quota Exhaustion (402)Your AI provider says your balance or credits are used up.Top up your provider account, then try again. Your search text is kept. Click Configure AI Settings to review your setup.
Invalid key / unauthorizedThe provider rejected your key.Re-enter the key in AI Settings.
TimeoutThe provider took longer than 15 seconds.Try again.
AI button unavailableAI features are part of the paid plan; your trial or subscription may have ended.Check Subscription & Billing.

#7. Privacy & Security

  • Your query text is sent to the provider you chose, under that provider's terms. Don't include confidential manuscript text in a query.
  • Biblion keeps your key out of its logs and never shows it in full.
  • Keys saved to your account are stored encrypted.
  • Sign Out clears your sign-in and AI keys from the browser, which protects you on shared computers.
